title: Reading the square control map

D0.outcome: Says that the control map shows, for every square, how many White and how many Black pieces attack it.

D1.outcome: Reads the n-m counts and the blue or orange tint on a given square, and names two things the map leaves out: pins and x-rays.

D2.outcome: Uses the map as a habit before moving: reads the landing square and the squares around the pieces first, then checks for pins and batteries by eye.

misconceptions: A piece the map counts as an attacker can always make the capture.
A higher number on the map means the side wins the exchange on that square.
The map shows every piece lined up on the square, including those behind another piece.
conditions: The map counts direct attacks only, and pins and the king's safety are ignored on purpose.
The map shows the position before you move; after a move the numbers on the squares you leave and enter change.
contrasts: The same 0-1 count on a square, once with the attacking knight pinned to its king and once with it free.
A queen with a rook behind it on the same file: the map counts one attacker, not two.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.CENTER.CONTROL.D1: the map is most useful for seeing who holds the centre, which that lesson explains
